questions.prompt: What is the capital city of Norway?

hints.nudge: A capital city is where a country’s government meets. The other three are capital cities too, of other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Norway article.

questions.proof: The capital is the city of Oslo.

questions.prompt: Which of these countries shares a border with Norway?

hints.nudge: Two countries are neighbours when you can walk from one into the other. Picture Norway on the globe and look at what it touches.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the “History” part of the Norway article.

questions.proof: In 1397, Denmark, Norway and Sweden began the Kalmar Union.

questions.prompt: Which language is an official language of Norway?

hints.nudge: An official language is the one used in schools, courts and government. The other three are spoken in other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the “Ethnicity” part of the Norway article.

questions.proof: Therefore, there are two standard languages, Bokmål and Nynorsk.

questions.prompt: Fill the gap: “The mainland of Norway is surrounded by the North Sea and Atlantic Ocean on the west side, and borders _____, Finland, and Sweden to the east.”

hints.nudge: In the sentence the missing word sits beside “borders”. It names one thing, not an action.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Norway article.

questions.proof: The mainland of Norway is surrounded by the North Sea and Atlantic Ocean on the west side, and borders Russia, Finland, and Sweden to the east.

questions.prompt: Fill the gap: “The Monarchy of Norway has been independent since _____.”

hints.nudge: It is a year in the nineteenth century.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Norway article.

questions.proof: The Monarchy of Norway has been independent since 1814.
